fields.description:
`_engine_support/reads.py:133-137` and `:151-157` print to stderr and call `sys.exit(1)` when the
repo root is not a git worktree. That function is reached from the library gate surface
(`_lib_gates.py:42,68,83,109,118,163,210`) and thence from MCP (`_mcp_reads.py:212,218,224`).

Empirically proven during verification: a real in-memory FastMCP client was driven against a tool
that exits this way. FastMCP catches `Exception` (`mcp/server/fastmcp/tools/base.py:116`) and
`SystemExit` is a `BaseException`, so the whole `anyio.run` dies — the MCP server PROCESS
terminates rather than returning a tool error.

Trigger is narrow (REBAR_ROOT unset with a non-repo cwd, or the repo vanishing mid-session), but a
leaf helper unilaterally deciding process lifetime for every embedding surface is the defect. The
library contract is to raise `RebarError`.

Both remediation proposers converged: convert to a domain exception and map it to exit 1 at the CLI
boundary ONLY, so the CLI's observable behaviour is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tracker_dir()` raises a rebar error instead of calling `sys.exit`
- [x] The CLI maps that error to exit 1 with the same message as today
- [x] A test asserts an MCP tool returns an error payload (not a dead server) with REBAR_ROOT unset in a non-repo cwd
- [x] No `sys.exit` remains reachable from `_lib_*` or `_mcp_*`
